title: Review lab playbook notes — Ava
content:
Quick context / intent:
- Personal lab for making a small, pragmatic playbook for mid-sized refactors (20–500 LOC changes across 2–6 files).
- Goal: reduce cognitive load during review, make reviewers ask better questions, speed up followups, and make rollbacks less painful.
- Not a team policy yet — this is my working notes. Will try with Samir on PR #4123 and iterate.

High level heuristics (ranked priority):
1) Safety first: can this change affect serving/runtime paths? If yes -> more integration tests + canary.
2) Observable impact: add a metric or log if behavior changes in prod (even a debug-level metric that can be removed).
3) Minimize scope: break into behavior-preserving refactor vs feature change. Separate into multiple PRs if both.
4) Tests: unit + lightweight integration; for infra/serving prefer deterministic infra tests (small cluster/job).
5) Reversibility: every nontrivial change needs an explicit rollback step in PR description.

Quick checklist (to paste into PR description) — keep short:
- Summary: single-sentence description of change and motivation.
- Risk category: low|medium|high (justify in 1 line).
- Surface area: list modules / routes / endpoints / data flows touched.
- Observability: metrics/logs added? trace points? link to dashboard if created.
- Rollout plan: canary % / duration / expected health signals.
- Rollback steps: exact commands or config switch names.
- Test matrix: unit/integration/e2e + manual smoke.
- Backcompat: yes/no + compatibility notes.
- Timebox: estimate review time and deploy window.

Refactor-specific notes / red flags:
- Hidden side-effects: watch for global mutable caches, singletons, env-dependent behavior.
- Thundering-cache risk: changes to KV/cache keys need migration plan.
- Latency regressions: any additional allocations/JSON copies inside hot path -> benchmark locally.
- Kernel/quantization edgecases: if touching model runtime glue, ensure not to change shape/order of KV cache.

Triage rubric for reviewer (fast lane vs deep dive):
- Fast lane (approve w/ light comments): cosmetic, naming, small extraction, tests included, no runtime surface change.
- Deep dive (request full review): touches serving/runtime, changes protocol/contract, migration needed, nontrivial concurrency changes.

Mini-experiment ideas (things to try on small PRs):
- Add a single "refactor metadata" header to PRs that exposes: risk label, rough perf impact, rollout suggestion. Track reviewer time vs similar PRs.
- Try a 2-reviewer rule for anything marked "medium" or "high" risk for two weeks. Measure throughput impact.
- Bake a tiny checklist bot comment that reminds author to include rollback steps and rollout plan.

Template snippets (one-line) to reuse:
- "Rollout: canary 10% for 2h observing error-rate/latency, then escalate to 50% for 2h, then full."
- "Rollback: revert rollout in console (route: /deployments/blue)/ or run infra rollback script: ./scripts/rollback.sh <id>"
- "Smoke test: call /health and run sample generation with prompt X (attach stdout)."
